question: An 80-year-old man with a history of hypertension, ischemic heart disease and COPD, who underwent a complete rectocolonoscopy due to rectal bleeding, with the following findings: polypoid lesion 3 cm in diameter located 10 cm from the anal margin, occupying the half of the circumference. Rest of exploration without findings until blind. In the polyp biopsy, an adenocarcinoma limited to the submucosa is seen. Endorectal ultrasound: uT1N0. Pelvic MRI: T1N0. TC: No evidence of disease at a distance. What will be the most likely therapeutic decision to be made in the Multidisciplinary Tumor Commission?

options.opb: Neoadjuvant radiotherapy and low anterior resection of the rectum by laparoscopy.
options.opd: Anterior low resection of laparotomic rectus.
options.ope: Anterior low resection of laparoscopic rectal route and adjuvant radiotherapy.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Polypoid lesion identified -> Biopsy reveals adenocarcinoma limited to submucosa -> Staging indicates uT1N0 -> No evidence of distant disease -> Surgical resection is indicated -> Low anterior resection is appropriate for T1N0 -> Confidence in low anterior resection as a treatment option is high -> 85%

CHAIN: Polypoid lesion found during colonoscopy -> Biopsy shows submucosal adenocarcinoma -> Staging confirms uT1N0 -> No metastasis detected on imaging -> Multidisciplinary team considers surgical options -> Neoadjuvant therapy not necessary for T1N0 -> Low anterior resection is a standard approach -> Confidence in low anterior resection is moderate -> 80%

CHAIN: Rectal adenocarcinoma diagnosed -> Limited to submucosa (uT1N0) -> No lymph node involvement -> Surgical intervention is required -> Transanal endoscopic microsurgery is less invasive -> May not achieve adequate margins for T1N0 -> Low anterior resection preferred for complete resection -> Confidence in low anterior resection is high -> 90%

CHAIN: Rectal cancer identified -> Staging shows uT1N0 -> No distant metastasis -> Surgical options evaluated by tumor board -> Abdominal-perineal resection is more invasive -> Low anterior resection is less invasive and effective -> Confidence in low anterior resection as a treatment option is high -> 85%
enhanced_information: The patient has a rectal adenocarcinoma classified as uT1N0, indicating it is limited to the submucosa with no lymph node involvement or distant metastasis. Surgical resection is the primary treatment for this stage of cancer. Low anterior resection (LAR) is the preferred surgical approach for T1N0 lesions, as it allows for adequate resection while preserving anal function. Transanal endoscopic microsurgery (TEM) may be considered for smaller lesions but may not ensure adequate margins for T1N0. Abdominal-perineal resection is more invasive and typically reserved for more advanced cases. Neoadjuvant therapy is not indicated for T1N0. Therefore, the most likely therapeutic decision by the Multidisciplinary Tumor Commission would be low anterior resection, supported by the consensus that this approach is effective and appropriate for the patient's staging.
analysis: The patient has a localized adenocarcinoma of the rectum (T1N0), which is limited to the submucosa and does not show any distant spread or lymph node involvement. Transanal endoscopic microsurgery (TEM) is a suitable option for early-stage rectal cancer as it is less invasive, preserves rectal function, and has a lower morbidity rate compared to more extensive surgeries like abdominal-perineal resection or low anterior resection. Given the patient's age and comorbidities, a less invasive procedure would likely be preferable to minimize operative risk and recovery time.
